qa.q: How can you find the longest ponytail in your class without a ruler?
qa.a: Stand the girls side by side and compare
qa.e: Comparing side by side shows which is longest.

qa.q: Raju's room is 12 footsteps long. Mira's room is 9 footsteps (same person). How many more footsteps is Raju's room?
Why do people get different hand-span counts for the same table?
qa.a: Their hands are of different sizes
qa.e: This is why we need a common unit everyone agrees on.

qa.q: What is the best way to compare paper strings?
qa.a: Line up one end of each and see where the other ends are
qa.e: Matching one end shows clearly which is longest.

qa.q: Rohit walks heel to toe across the room: 20 steps. Asha walks with big gaps: 14 steps. Whose count is better?
qa.a: Rohit's, as there are no gaps
qa.e: Heel-to-toe has no gaps, so it measures correctly.

qa.q: A rope fits 6 times between two walls. Another rope twice as long would fit how many times?
qa.e: A longer rope fits fewer times: 6 ÷ 2 = 3.

qa.q: A board border needs 5 strings on the top, 5 on the bottom and 3 on each side. How many strings?
Which method gives the SAME answer for everyone measuring a wall?
qa.e: Everyone using the same stick gets the same count.

qa.q: Strings: red 7 spans, blue 4 spans, green 9 spans. Which is shortest?
qa.e: 4 spans is the smallest.

qa.q: Same strings (7, 4, 9 spans). How many spans longer is green than blue?
Ram lays a stick 8 times along a wall but the stick overlaps a bit each time. Is the real length more or less than 8 sticks?
qa.e: Overlaps mean each stick covers less new wall, so 8 sticks cover less than 8 full lengths. The wall is less than 8 sticks long.

qa.q: A line is 6 boxes long. Which thread matches it?
qa.e: Same length means same number of boxes.

qa.q: Draw a string longer than a 4-box string. How many boxes could it be?
qa.e: 6 is more than 4.

qa.q: Draw a string shorter than an 8-box string. How many boxes could it be?
qa.e: 5 is less than 8.

qa.q: A moustache's left half is 4 boxes. The right half is 3 boxes. How many boxes must be added to the right?
Three strings are lined up at one end. Red ends at 9, blue at 12, green at 10. Which is longest?
qa.e: 12 goes furthest.

qa.q: A full moustache has two equal halves of 5 boxes each. How many boxes long is it in all?
Mohan starts his thread a little after the start of the line and cuts at the end of the line. His thread is…
qa.e: He started late, so his thread misses a bit at the start.

qa.q: Raju's string is 3 boxes longer than a 6-box string. How many boxes long is Raju's string?
How can you compare the width of a table and a door without moving the table?
qa.a: Use a string to measure one and compare with the other
qa.e: The string carries the length across.

qa.q: The string for the table is shorter than the door's width. What does this tell us?
qa.e: The door is wider than the table.

qa.q: A bridge has a gap 5 blocks high. A toy is 3 blocks tall. Can it pass?
qa.e: 3 is less than 5, so it fits under.

qa.q: A gap under the bridge is 4 blocks high. Which toy CANNOT pass?
qa.e: 6 is more than 4.

qa.q: A pole is 7 sticks tall and the gate is 5 sticks tall. How many sticks too tall is the pole to pass standing up?
Which might NOT pass through a school gate?
qa.e: A truck is too tall and wide for most school gates.

qa.q: Raju's string matches his window's width. It is longer than Mira's window. Whose window is wider?
qa.e: Raju's window is as wide as the string, and the string is longer than Mira's window.

qa.q: Why do we need a third object like a string?
qa.a: When two things cannot be put side by side
qa.e: It lets us compare lengths in different places.

qa.q: How can you test if your arm span equals your height?
qa.a: Measure both with a string and compare
qa.e: A string shows both lengths so you can compare them.

qa.q: How can you check if your head is about 3 hand spans around?
qa.a: Wrap a string around your head and measure it in spans
qa.e: The string gives the distance around, and then we measure it with spans.

qa.q: Forearm means…
qa.e: The forearm is the part from the elbow to the wrist.

qa.q: 15 children test 'forearm = foot'. 12 say yes. How many say no?
In the test above, is 'forearm = foot' true for ALL 15 children?
qa.e: All means every one. 3 did not fit.

qa.q: Riya's head is 3 spans around. Her brother's head is also 3 of HIS spans. Are their heads the same size?
qa.a: Not necessarily: their spans may be different
qa.e: 3 spans each, but spans are different sizes.

qa.q: Which is the best way to test an idea about body measures?
qa.a: Try it on many people and record
qa.e: Many people give a fairer answer.

qa.q: 6 friends tested arm span = height. All 6 said yes. Can we be sure it is true for every person in the world?
qa.e: It is true for these 6, but other people may be different.

qa.q: Why do we need a standard unit like the metre?
qa.a: So everyone gets the same measure
qa.e: Body units differ, but a metre is the same for all.

qa.q: Which tool shows 1 metre?
qa.e: A metre rod is exactly 1 metre long.

qa.q: How do you make a 1-metre rope?
qa.a: Lay it along a metre rod and cut at the end
qa.e: Matching it to the metre rod makes it exactly 1 metre.

qa.q: A mat is 2 m long. Three mats in a row are how long?
Ravi stands against a 1-metre mark on the wall. His head is above the mark. What does this tell us?
qa.e: Above the mark means taller.

qa.q: A rope is 5 m long. 2 m is cut off. How much is left?
Which is about 1 metre long?
qa.a: A big stride of a grown-up
qa.e: A big stride is about 1 metre.

qa.q: Tina measures her room with a metre tape: 4 m. Her friend measures it with the same tape. What will the friend get?
qa.e: A standard unit gives the same answer for everyone.

qa.q: Which is longer than 1 metre?
qa.e: A door is about 2 metres tall.

qa.q: Which is shorter than 1 metre?
qa.e: A notebook is much shorter than a metre.

qa.q: Which is about 1 metre?
qa.e: A metre rod is exactly 1 metre.

qa.q: In a class, 18 children are taller than 1 m and 7 are shorter. How many children?
Same class: how many more are taller than 1 m than shorter?
Ajay's head is below the 1-metre mark. He is…
qa.e: Below the mark means shorter.

qa.q: A bed is about 2 m long. Is that more or less than 1 metre?
qa.e: 2 metres is more than 1 metre.

qa.q: Which list has ONLY things longer than 1 metre?
qa.e: A bus, a door and a bed are all longer than 1 m.

qa.q: How do you make a half-metre rope from a 1-metre rope?
qa.a: Fold it in half and cut
qa.e: Folding in half gives two equal halves.

qa.q: How many half metres make 1 metre?
qa.e: 2 halves make a whole.

qa.q: How many quarter metres make 1 metre?
qa.e: 4 quarters make a whole.

qa.q: How many quarter metres make a half metre?
qa.e: 2 quarters = 1 half.

qa.q: Which is about half a metre long?
qa.e: A school bag is about half a metre tall.

qa.q: Which is LESS than a quarter metre?
qa.e: An eraser is very small.

qa.q: A throw is measured with 3 metre ropes and 1 half-metre rope. How far?
qa.e: 3 m + half m = 3 and a half m.

qa.q: A ribbon is 4 quarter metres long. How long is it?
qa.e: 4 quarters make 1 whole metre.

qa.q: How many cuts make 4 equal pieces of a rope?
qa.e: Pieces − 1 = cuts. 4 − 1 = 3.

qa.q: How many pieces do 2 cuts make?
qa.e: Cuts + 1 = pieces.

qa.q: Sita's guessed thread is a bit longer than the metre rod. What was her estimate?
qa.e: Longer than the rod means more than 1 m.

qa.q: Kabir takes 5 footsteps to cover 1 metre. How many footsteps for 3 metres?
A metre rope is laid along a wall 8 times. How long is the wall?
qa.e: Each lay is 1 metre: 8 × 1 = 8 m.

qa.q: Why might Ria and her teacher take different numbers of steps to make 1 metre?
qa.e: Bigger steps mean fewer steps.

qa.q: A ribbon is cut into 10 equal pieces. How many cuts?
Raju's estimate of 1 metre was exactly as long as the metre rod. What does this mean?
qa.e: Same length as the rod means exactly 1 metre.

qa.q: What comes next? 5, 10, 15, 20, ___
qa.e: The rule is 'add 5'. 20 + 5 = 25.

qa.q: What is the rule? 30, 27, 24, 21
qa.e: Each number is 3 less than the one before: 30 − 3 = 27, 27 − 3 = 24.

qa.q: Find the missing number: 6, 12, ___, 24, 30
qa.e: The rule is 'add 6'. 12 + 6 = 18, and 18 + 6 = 24.

qa.q: What comes next? 1, 4, 7, 10, ___
qa.e: The rule is 'add 3'. 10 + 3 = 13.

qa.q: Which number is EVEN?
qa.e: Even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. 58 ends in 8.

qa.q: At the party, Riya puts 2 balloons on the first chair, 4 on the second and 6 on the third. How many on the fourth chair?
qa.e: The rule is 'add 2'. 6 + 2 = 8.

qa.q: What comes next? 50, 40, 30, ___
qa.e: The rule is 'take away 10'. 30 − 10 = 20.

qa.q: Arjun's pattern is 2, 4, 8, 16, ___. Each number is double the one before. What comes next?
qa.e: Double 16 is 16 + 16 = 32.

qa.q: What comes next? 🔴🟢🔴🟢🔴___
qa.e: The core is 🔴🟢. After 🔴 comes 🟢.

qa.q: Bangles go: red, red, gold, red, red, gold. What is the core of this pattern?
qa.e: The part that repeats is red, red, gold.

qa.q: Rangoli dots go: 1 dot, 3 dots, 5 dots, 7 dots. How many dots come next?
qa.e: Each step adds 2 dots. 7 + 2 = 9.

qa.q: A paper chain goes pink, blue, pink, blue ... What colour is the 8th ring?
qa.e: Pink is in places 1, 3, 5, 7. Blue is in places 2, 4, 6, 8. So the 8th ring is blue.

qa.q: Which of these is a GROWING pattern?
qa.e: In ⭐, ⭐⭐, ⭐⭐⭐ each step has one more star, so it grows.

qa.q: Kabir sets plates: big, small, small, big, small, small, big, ___. What comes next?
qa.e: The core is big, small, small. After 'big' comes 'small'.

qa.q: Tiles: step 1 has 2 tiles, step 2 has 4 tiles, step 3 has 6 tiles. How many tiles in step 4?
qa.e: Each step adds 2 tiles. 6 + 2 = 8.

qa.q: A border goes triangle, circle, square, triangle, circle, square ... Which shape is 7th?
qa.e: The core has 3 shapes. Places 1, 4 and 7 are triangles.

qa.q: What do we call the fold line that splits a shape into two matching halves?
qa.e: A line of symmetry divides a shape into two halves that are mirror images.

qa.q: Which letter is symmetrical?
qa.e: Fold H down the middle and both halves match. F, G and R do not have matching halves.

qa.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
qa.e: A square can be folded top to bottom, side to side and along both corner-to-corner lines. That makes 4.

qa.q: Riya folds a paper heart down the middle and the two halves match. The heart is ___.
qa.e: When two halves match exactly after folding, the shape is symmetrical.

qa.q: Which of these is NOT symmetrical?
qa.e: J has a hook on one side only, so no fold makes its halves match.

qa.q: How many lines of symmetry does a long rectangle, like a door, have?
qa.e: Folding down the middle and across the middle both work. Corner-to-corner folds do not.

qa.q: Aisha drew half of a rangoli flower. To make it symmetrical, the other half must be ___.
qa.a: a mirror copy of the first half
qa.e: In a symmetrical design, one half is a mirror image of the other.

qa.q: Which word is made ONLY of letters that match when folded down the middle?
qa.e: T, O, M and A all match when folded down the middle. MANGO has N and G, CAKE has C, K and E, PIZZA has P and Z. These do not.

qa.q: Chintu's glass is bigger than Mintu's. Who needs fewer glasses to fill a bucket?
qa.e: A bigger glass holds more, so fewer are needed.

qa.q: A pot fills 8 glasses. A jug fills 5 of the same glasses. How many more glasses does the pot fill?
Bottle A fills 7 cups, bottle B fills 9 cups and bottle C fills 4 cups. Which holds the MOST?
qa.e: 9 cups is the most.

qa.q: Same bottles (7, 9, 4 cups). Which holds the LEAST?
qa.e: 4 cups is the least.

qa.q: To compare a bottle and a jug fairly, what should we pour them into?
qa.e: The same-sized glass is a fair unit.

qa.q: A tank fills 20 big buckets or 40 small buckets. Which bucket holds more?
qa.e: Fewer big buckets are needed, so each holds more.

qa.q: A tall, thin glass and a short, wide bowl. How can we be sure which holds more?
qa.a: Fill one and pour into the other
qa.e: Pouring tests it. Height alone can fool us.

qa.q: Jug fills 6 glasses. Pot fills twice as many. How many glasses does the pot fill?
Which of these holds the MOST water?
qa.e: A bucket is much bigger inside than a cup, spoon or glass, so it holds the most.

qa.q: Which unit do we use to measure milk?
qa.e: Liquids like milk are measured in litres.

qa.q: One jug of water fills 5 glasses. How many glasses do 2 jugs fill?
qa.e: 2 jugs fill 5 + 5 = 10 glasses.

qa.q: How many millilitres are there in 1 litre?
qa.e: 1 litre = 1000 millilitres.

qa.q: Riya's bottle holds 2 litres of water. She drinks 1 litre. How much water is left?
qa.e: 2 litres − 1 litre = 1 litre.

qa.q: A water tank holds 50 buckets of water. 20 buckets are used. How many buckets of water are left?
qa.e: 50 − 20 = 30 buckets are left.

qa.q: Kabir pours a full bottle of water into an empty mug, and the mug overflows. What does this tell us?
qa.a: The bottle holds more than the mug
qa.e: The mug could not hold all the water from the bottle, so the bottle holds more.

qa.q: Half a litre is how many millilitres?
qa.e: 1 litre is 1000 mL. Half of 1000 is 500.

qa.q: 1 jug fills 4 glasses. How many glasses do 3 jugs fill?
1 glass takes 5 ladles. How many ladles for 4 glasses?
A bucket is filled with a mug and with a glass. The glass is smaller. Which needs more fills?
qa.e: A smaller vessel needs more fills.

qa.q: Raju guessed 6 cups fill a jug. When he poured, it took 8 cups. How far off was his guess?
Which is best to serve dal at lunch?
qa.e: A ladle serves a small amount neatly.

qa.q: 18 glasses of water are needed. 1 jug fills 6 glasses. How many jugs?
A pot holds 10 bowls of rice. A bowl holds 2 ladles. How many ladles fill the pot?
qa.e: 10 bowls × 2 ladles = 20.

qa.q: Bottle A fills 3 glasses. Bottle B fills 3 cups. Can we say they hold the same?
qa.a: No, glasses and cups may be different sizes
qa.e: We can compare only with the same unit.

qa.q: Why does a milkman use a measuring can?
qa.a: So everyone gets the same amount
qa.e: A standard measure gives a fair, equal amount.

qa.q: Which is measured in litres?
qa.e: Litres measure liquids.

qa.q: Which holds MORE than 1 litre?
qa.e: A bucket holds many litres.

qa.q: Which holds LESS than 1 litre?
qa.e: A glass holds much less than a litre.

qa.q: Tina guessed her bucket holds 10 L. She poured in 1-litre bottles 13 times to fill it. How far off was she?
A family uses 6 litres of water in the morning and 8 litres in the evening for plants. How much in all?
Which is a good way to save water?
qa.e: Closing the tap saves many litres.

qa.q: A water can holds 20 L. How many 1-litre bottles can it fill?
qa.e: Each bottle takes 1 L. 20 L fills 20 bottles.

qa.q: How many half-litre bottles make 1 litre?
qa.e: Half + half = 1 whole.

qa.q: How many quarter-litre cups make 1 litre?
qa.e: 4 quarters = 1 whole.

qa.q: How many quarter litres make half a litre?
qa.e: 2 quarters = 1 half.

qa.q: Mummy buys 3 half-litre packets of milk. How many litres is that?
qa.e: 2 half-litres = 1 litre, plus 1 more half.

qa.q: A jug holds 2 litres. How many half-litre glasses can it fill?
qa.e: Each litre fills 2 half-litre glasses. 2 + 2 = 4.

qa.q: A 1-litre bottle is poured into quarter-litre cups. 3 are filled. How many more cups are needed to empty it?
Which is more: half a litre or a quarter litre?
qa.e: Half is 2 quarters, so it is more.

qa.q: Raju drinks 2 quarter-litre glasses of milk. How much milk is that?
qa.e: 2 quarters = half.

qa.q: Riya holds a brick in one hand and a sponge in the other. Which hand goes down more?
qa.e: The brick is heavier, so it pulls down more.

qa.q: A pencil box balances 12 coins. A sharpener balances 3 coins. How many more coins does the box weigh?
A pan balance shows a ball and 8 erasers balancing. A toy balances 5 erasers. Which is heavier?
qa.e: 8 erasers is more than 5.

qa.q: Which units are good for weighing small things on a pan balance?
qa.e: Same-kind coins weigh the same each, so they are a fair unit.

qa.q: Order from lightest: mango 10 coins, guava 7 coins, papaya 30 coins.
Bag A has 6 books and bag B has 2 (same books). How many books should move from A to B to make them equal?
qa.e: 6 + 2 = 8, so 4 each. Move 6 − 4 = 2.

qa.q: Kabir records: 'Bat or ball? Bat heavier. Shoe or sock? Shoe heavier.' How many pairs did he record?
qa.e: Bat-ball and shoe-sock: 2 pairs.

qa.q: A matchbox of sand balances 1 eraser. A book balances 9 matchboxes. How many erasers does the book balance?
qa.e: Each matchbox = 1 eraser, so 9 matchboxes = 9 erasers.

qa.q: On a balance, which side goes down?
qa.e: The heavier object pulls its side of the balance down.

qa.q: Which of these is the heaviest?
qa.e: A brick is made of hard, packed clay, so it is much heavier than the others.

qa.q: Which unit is used to weigh a sack of rice?
qa.e: Weight is measured in kilograms. Litres are for liquids.

qa.q: How many grams make 1 kilogram?
qa.e: 1 kilogram = 1000 grams.

qa.q: Meena buys 2 kg of onions and 3 kg of potatoes. What is the total weight?
qa.e: 2 kg + 3 kg = 5 kg.

qa.q: A balloon and a marble are put on a balance. The marble's side goes down. Which is lighter?
qa.e: The lighter side goes up. The marble went down, so the balloon is lighter.

qa.q: Arjun weighs 25 kg. His little sister weighs 15 kg. How much heavier is Arjun?
qa.e: Find the difference: 25 kg − 15 kg = 10 kg.

qa.q: A bag of atta weighs 5 kg. Nani Maa uses 2 kg to make rotis. How much atta is left?
qa.e: 5 kg − 2 kg = 3 kg.

qa.q: Which is likely to weigh about 1 kg?
qa.a: A packet of sugar marked 1 kg
qa.e: The packet is marked 1 kg.

qa.q: Which is HEAVIER than 1 kg?
qa.e: A big watermelon weighs a few kilograms.

qa.q: Which is LIGHTER than 1 kg?
qa.e: An eraser weighs very little.

qa.q: How many half-kilograms make 1 kg?
qa.e: Half + half = 1.

qa.q: How many quarter-kilograms make 1 kg?
qa.e: 4 quarters = 1 whole.

qa.q: How many quarter-kilograms make half a kilogram?
qa.e: 2 quarters = 1 half.

qa.q: Mummy buys 1 kg of tomatoes using only quarter-kg weights. How many weights does the seller use?
qa.e: 4 × quarter kg = 1 kg.

qa.q: A small papaya balances a half-kg weight. Two such papayas weigh about…
qa.e: Half + half = 1 kg.

qa.q: A dairy has 30 litres of milk. It sells 18 litres. How much milk is left?
qa.e: 'Left' means take away. 30 − 18 = 12 litres.

qa.q: A water cooler holds 4 litres. It is filled 3 times in a day. How much water is that?
qa.e: 3 times 4 litres: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 litres.

qa.q: Harpreet buys 5 kg of rice and 2 kg of sugar. How many kilograms is that in all?
qa.e: 'In all' means add. 5 kg + 2 kg = 7 kg.

qa.q: Riya fills a 10-litre bucket using a 2-litre jug. How many jugfuls does she pour?
qa.e: Count by 2s to 10: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. That is 5 jugfuls.

qa.q: A shopkeeper has 25 kg of potatoes. He sells 10 kg in the morning and 5 kg in the evening. How much is left?
qa.e: Take away both amounts: 25 − 10 = 15, then 15 − 5 = 10 kg.

qa.q: Kabir's mother bought 3 bags of flour. Each bag weighs 5 kg. What is the total weight?
qa.e: 3 bags of 5 kg: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15 kg.

qa.q: A tank had 40 litres of water. 15 litres were used to water the plants. How many litres are left?
qa.e: 40 − 15: take away 10 to get 30, then 5 more to get 25 litres.

qa.q: Which of these should be measured in kilograms?
qa.e: Apples are solid things, so we weigh them in kilograms. The others are liquids, measured in litres.

qa.q: Three balls, one is heavier. You put ball 1 and ball 2 on the pans. They balance. Which is heavier?
qa.e: Balls 1 and 2 weigh the same, so the heavy one is the one kept aside.

qa.q: Three balls, one is heavier. Ball A goes down against ball B. Which is heavier?
qa.e: The side that goes down is heavier.

qa.q: How many times must you use the balance to find the heavy ball among 3?
qa.e: One weighing is enough with the trick.

qa.q: P is heavier than Q. Q is heavier than R. Which is lightest?
qa.e: P > Q > R, so R is lightest.

qa.q: X is lighter than Y. Z is heavier than Y. Order from heaviest.
qa.e: Z > Y and Y > X, so Z, Y, X.

qa.q: If pans balance with ball M on one and ball N on the other, what is true?
qa.a: M and N weigh the same
qa.e: Balanced pans mean equal weight.

qa.q: The pan with ball K goes UP. What does this tell us about K?
qa.e: The lighter side goes up.

qa.q: A > B and A > C. Can we tell which of B and C is heavier?
qa.a: No, we must weigh B and C
qa.e: We only know A is the heaviest. One more weighing compares B and C.

qa.q: Kishan has 364 rose plants and gets 52 more. How many now?
What is 245 + 38?
qa.e: 5 + 8 = 13: 3 ones, carry 1 ten. 4 + 3 + 1 = 8 tens. 2 hundreds.

qa.q: In a box diagram, the parts are 523 and 64. What goes in the whole box?
Kishan sold 178 plants on Monday and 45 on Tuesday. How many in all?
qa.e: 8 + 5 = 13, carry 1. 7 + 4 + 1 = 12 tens, carry 1. 1 + 1 = 2 hundreds.

qa.q: Which story fits a box diagram with parts 312 and 25?
qa.a: 312 marigolds and 25 roses. How many plants?
qa.e: Two parts joined to find the whole.

qa.q: What is 690 + 10?
qa.e: 69 tens + 1 ten = 70 tens = 700.

qa.q: A nursery has 456 pots. 87 more arrive. How many pots now?
qa.e: 6 + 7 = 13, carry 1. 5 + 8 + 1 = 14 tens, carry 1. 4 + 1 = 5 hundreds.

qa.q: Which is the missing part? Whole 450, part 420.
What is 230 − 75?
qa.e: Break a ten and a hundred: 155.

qa.q: When there are not enough ones, what do we break?
qa.e: 1 ten = 10 ones.

qa.q: 1 hundred flat is broken. How many ten rods do we get?
qa.e: 1 hundred = 10 tens.

qa.q: What is 342 − 18?
What is 405 − 60?
qa.e: 0 tens − 6 tens: break a hundred. 10 − 6 = 4 tens. 3 hundreds. 5 ones.

qa.q: After breaking 1 ten, 4 tens 3 ones becomes…
qa.e: 1 ten moves to the ones: 3 tens and 13 ones. The value is still 43.

qa.q: A nursery had 500 saplings and sold 125. How many are left?
Check 230 − 75 = 155 by adding back.
qa.e: Adding the part back should give the whole.

qa.q: What is 476 + 10?
qa.e: Adding 10 increases the tens digit by 1.

qa.q: What is 476 + 100?
qa.e: Adding 100 increases the hundreds digit by 1.

qa.q: On the 451-530 grid, what is just below 463?
qa.e: Down a row adds 10.

qa.q: What is 489 + 1?
Solve 364 + 52 with jumps: 364 + 50 = 414. Then?
On a number line, 230 − 70 = 160. Then 160 − 5 = ?
Which number is 1 more than 529?
Start at 512. Add 10 three times. Where are you?
What is barter?
qa.e: Barter is a direct swap of goods.

qa.q: Why is barter difficult?
qa.a: The other person may not want what you have
qa.e: Both people must want each other's things.

qa.q: Why do we use money?
qa.a: Everyone accepts it and it has fixed values
qa.e: Money is accepted by all and makes trade easy.

qa.q: Which costs more: a ₹45 kite or a ₹54 kite?
A toy costs ₹120 and a ball costs ₹85. How much more is the toy?
Which is the cheapest?
qa.e: ₹15 is the least.

qa.q: A farmer swaps 2 sacks of wheat for 1 goat. How many goats for 6 sacks?
qa.e: 2 sacks per goat. 6 ÷ 2 = 3 goats.

qa.q: Which has the greater value?
qa.e: ₹100 is more than ₹50, ₹50 and ₹40.

qa.q: Riya has three ₹10 notes. How much money does she have?
qa.e: Count by 10s three times: 10, 20, 30.

qa.q: How many ₹5 coins make ₹20?
qa.e: Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 coins.

qa.q: Arjun has one ₹100 note, one ₹20 note and two ₹2 coins. How much money does he have?
Which group of coins makes ₹10?
qa.e: ₹5 + ₹5 = ₹10. Three ₹2 coins make ₹6, two ₹2 coins make ₹4, and one ₹5 coin is ₹5.

qa.q: How many ₹50 notes make ₹200?
qa.e: Count by 50s: 50, 100, 150, 200. That is 4 notes.

qa.q: Kabir counts his money: ₹50, ₹20, ₹20, ₹10 and ₹5. How much is it in all?
qa.e: Start with ₹50, then count on: 70, 90, 100, 105.

qa.q: Which notes make exactly ₹70?
Meena has two ₹10 coins and three ₹2 coins. How much money does she have?
qa.e: Two ₹10 coins = ₹20. Three ₹2 coins = ₹6. ₹20 + ₹6 = ₹26.

qa.q: How many ₹100 notes make ₹500?
Riya has 3 ₹100 notes. How many more ₹100 notes make ₹500?
Which makes ₹500?
Whose picture is on Indian notes?
qa.e: Mahatma Gandhi's picture is on our notes.

qa.q: How is the value shown on a note?
qa.e: Both numbers and words are printed.

qa.q: Why do some notes have raised marks?
qa.a: To help people who cannot see well
qa.e: People can feel the marks to know the value.

qa.q: Leela changes a ₹500 note into ₹50 notes. How many notes does she get?
Arjun has two ₹200 notes. How much money is that?
A notebook costs ₹30 and a pen costs ₹15. What is the total cost?
qa.e: Add the prices: ₹30 + ₹15 = ₹45.

qa.q: Aisha buys 4 bananas at ₹5 each. How much does she pay?
qa.e: 4 bananas at ₹5 each: 5, 10, 15, 20.

qa.q: At a mela, Joseph buys a toy for ₹85 and a balloon for ₹15. How much does he spend?
A bill says: Rice ₹60, Dal ₹45, Salt ₹20. What is the total?
Kabir wants a cricket ball that costs ₹48. He has ₹50. Does he have enough money?
qa.e: ₹50 is more than ₹48, so he has enough. He will get ₹2 back.

qa.q: Riya buys 2 rakhis at ₹25 each. How much does she pay?
A plate of chole bhature costs ₹70 and a glass of lassi costs ₹30. What is the total cost?
qa.e: 7 tens + 3 tens = 10 tens = ₹100.

qa.q: Meena's mother buys 2 kg of tomatoes at ₹40 for each kg. How much does she pay?
qa.e: ₹40 for each kg, and she buys 2 kg: ₹40 + ₹40 = ₹80.

qa.q: Harpreet pays ₹50 for a toy that costs ₹35. How much change does she get?
qa.e: Change = ₹50 − ₹35 = ₹15. Count up: 35 to 40 is 5, 40 to 50 is 10.

qa.q: Kabir pays ₹100 for a book that costs ₹65. What is his change?
Joseph pays ₹20 for a juice that costs ₹12. What change does he get?
Aisha buys a pencil box for ₹28 and pays with ₹30. How much change does she get?
qa.e: ₹30 − ₹28 = ₹2. From 28, two steps reach 30.

qa.q: Riya pays ₹100 for two things that cost ₹40 and ₹30. How much change does she get?
qa.e: First find the total: ₹40 + ₹30 = ₹70. Then change = ₹100 − ₹70 = ₹30.

qa.q: Meena paid ₹50 and got ₹15 change. How much did her things cost?
qa.e: Price = money given − change = ₹50 − ₹15 = ₹35. Check: ₹35 + ₹15 = ₹50.

qa.q: Arjun has a ₹200 note. He buys shoes for ₹150. How much change does he get?
Which is the right way to find change?
qa.e: Change is the extra money you gave, so take the price away from the money given.

qa.q: Ravi saves ₹45, ₹60 and ₹75. What is his total?
Mina saves ₹50 every week for 5 weeks. How much?
Ravi has ₹180. The bat costs ₹200. How much more?
Which shows ₹235?
Week 1: ₹120. Week 2: ₹95. Total?
Asha wants ₹400. She has saved ₹325. How much more?
Sohan has one ₹100 note, six ₹10 notes and four ₹1 coins. How much?
Ravi saves ₹30 a week. After how many weeks will he have ₹150?
What is 389 to the nearest hundred?
qa.e: 389 is closer to 400 than to 300.

qa.q: Estimate 389 + 214.
Estimate 712 − 289.
What is 650 to the nearest hundred?
qa.e: When the tens digit is 5, we round up.

qa.q: Which is the best estimate for 198 + 403?
Riya estimated 456 + 238 as 700. What did she do?
Is 345 + 362 more or less than 800?
qa.e: About 300 + 400 = 700. Exactly, it is 707, less than 800.

qa.q: Estimate 905 − 499.
Without adding, which is greater?
qa.e: Both have 456. 120 is more than 102.

qa.q: Without subtracting, which is greater?
qa.e: Taking away less leaves more.

qa.q: Which pair has equal value?
qa.e: Both are 350.
Order does not change a sum, so the missing number is 250.
1 moved from 51 to 199: 200 + 50.

qa.q: Which is SMALLER?
qa.e: Taking away 250 leaves less than taking away 205.
2 moved from 152 to 348. Both are 500.

qa.q: With cards 0-5 used once, which pair gives the BIGGEST sum?
qa.e: Biggest digits in the hundreds: 5 and 4. Then 3 and 2. 951.

qa.q: What is 531 + 420?
What is 301 − 254?
What is 825 + 175?
What is 600 − 82?
For the biggest sum, where should the biggest digits go?
qa.e: Hundreds are worth the most.

qa.q: Cards 2, 5, 8, 1, 4, 7. Make the biggest 3-digit number from three of them.
qa.e: Choose the 3 biggest: 8, 7, 5 in that order.

qa.q: Mentally: 999 + 1 − 500?
The 1st of a month is a Monday. Which date is the first Sunday?
qa.e: Monday 1, Tuesday 2, ... Sunday 7.

qa.q: A 30-day month starts on Monday. How many Mondays does it have?
A 31-day month starts on Monday. What day is the 31st?
qa.e: 29 is a Monday, 30 a Tuesday, 31 a Wednesday.

qa.q: Dates of all Thursdays in a month are 4, 11, 18, ___. What comes next?
School closes after the 10th for 12 days. On which date does it reopen?
qa.e: Holidays are 11th to 22nd (12 days), so it reopens on the 23rd.

qa.q: When making a calendar, the 1st falls on Wednesday. On which day does the 3rd fall?
qa.e: Wed 1, Thu 2, Fri 3.

qa.q: The 6th is a Saturday. What day is the 20th?
qa.e: 6 + 7 = 13 and 13 + 7 = 20, so it is also a Saturday.

qa.q: A shop is shut every Sunday. In a month the Sundays are 3, 10, 17, 24 and 31. How many days is the shop shut?
qa.e: There are 5 Sundays.

qa.q: How many days are there in a week?
qa.e: Monday to Sunday makes 7 days.

qa.q: How many months are there in a year?
qa.e: January to December makes 12 months.

qa.q: Which month comes right after June?
qa.e: The months go ... May, June, July, August ... So July comes after June.

qa.q: How many days does April have?
qa.e: April is one of the four months with 30 days: April, June, September and November.

qa.q: Today is Friday. What day will it be tomorrow?
qa.e: After Friday comes Saturday.

qa.q: If the 5th of a month is a Tuesday, what day is the 12th of the same month?
qa.e: 12 − 5 = 7 days, which is 1 week. So the 12th is also a Tuesday.

qa.q: Which month has only 28 days in most years?
qa.e: February is the shortest month. It has 28 days, and 29 in a leap year.

qa.q: Kabir's holiday is 2 weeks long. How many days is that?
qa.e: 1 week is 7 days, so 2 weeks is 7 + 7 = 14 days.

qa.q: How many days are in a year that is not a leap year?
qa.e: A normal year has 365 days.

qa.q: How many days does a leap year have?
qa.e: February gets an extra day: 366.

qa.q: About how many weeks are in a year?
Which stays the same every year?
qa.e: January to December, always in the same order.

qa.q: Which changes from year to year?
qa.e: Holi follows the moon calendar, so its date changes.

qa.q: How many days are left over after 52 full weeks in a 365-day year?
In a leap year, how many days does February have?
qa.e: In a leap year February has 29 days.

qa.q: Riya's birthday was on a Tuesday this year. The next year is not a leap year. On which day will it most likely be next year?
qa.e: 365 days = 52 weeks and 1 day, so the day moves 1 ahead.

qa.q: Arjun was born in 2018. How old is he in 2026, after his birthday?
Didi is twice as old as Raju and 10 years older. How old is Raju?
qa.e: If Raju is 10, Didi is 20: twice and 10 more.

qa.q: Same puzzle: how old is Didi?
Mother is twice as old as her son and 30 years older. How old is the son?
qa.e: If the son is 30, the mother is 60. 60 is twice 30 and 30 more.

qa.q: Sita is 9 and her brother is 4. How much older is Sita?
Sita is 9 and her brother is 4. In 3 years, how much older will Sita be?
qa.e: The gap stays the same: 5.

qa.q: Nani was born in 1960. How old is she in 2026, after her birthday?
Dev will be 10 next year. How old is he now?
In 14/11/2018, what is the month?
qa.e: The middle number 11 is the 11th month: November.

qa.q: Which is 2 October 2019 written as day/month/year?
qa.e: Day 02, month 10, year 2019.

qa.q: Born on 05/09/2016. How old in 2026 after the birthday?
Born on 05/09/2016. On which date is the birthday each year?
qa.e: 05 is the day and 09 is September.

qa.q: How many months from 5 March to 5 July?
qa.e: April, May, June, July: 4 months.

qa.q: How many days from 3 June to 20 June?
Which month is 12 in a date like 25/12/2019?
qa.e: The 12th month is December.

qa.q: Leela started school on 01/06/2022 and was born on 01/06/2018. How many years old was she when she started?
Meera is making her own page of important dates, like a birth certificate. Which of these should she write on it?
qa.e: A birth certificate records the date of birth. Meera can also add other important dates, like her first day at school.

qa.q: The short hand is on 3 and the long hand is on 12. What time is it?
qa.e: The long hand on 12 means o'clock. The short hand on 3 means 3. So it is 3 o'clock.

qa.q: Which hand of a clock shows the hours?
qa.e: The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes.

qa.q: How many minutes are there in 1 hour?
qa.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. The long hand takes 60 minutes to go all the way round.

qa.q: Riya's school bus comes at half past 7. Where is the long hand?
qa.e: At half past, the long hand is halfway round the clock, on 6.

qa.q: Cricket practice starts at 4 o'clock and ends at 5 o'clock. How long is the practice?
qa.e: From 4 o'clock to 5 o'clock the short hand moves 1 number. That is 1 hour.

qa.q: The long hand is on 6 and the short hand is between 11 and 12. What time is it?
qa.e: The long hand on 6 means half past. The short hand has passed 11, so it is half past 11.

qa.q: How many minutes are there in half an hour?
qa.e: Half of 60 minutes is 30 minutes.

qa.q: Arjun wakes up at 6 o'clock. He takes 1 hour to get ready. At what time is he ready?
qa.e: 1 hour after 6 o'clock is 7 o'clock.

qa.q: The long hand is on 3 and the short hand is just after 2. What time is it?
qa.e: The long hand on 3 means quarter past. The short hand just after 2 means it is quarter past 2.

qa.q: Where is the long hand at quarter to 6?
qa.e: At quarter to, the long hand is on 9, 15 minutes before the next hour.

qa.q: How many minutes is a quarter of an hour?
qa.e: 1 hour is 60 minutes. Share 60 into 4 equal parts: 15 minutes each.

qa.q: Quarter past 4 is the same as ___.
qa.e: Quarter past 4 is 15 minutes after 4 o'clock, written 4:15.

qa.q: Quarter to 9 is the same as ___.
qa.e: Quarter to 9 is 15 minutes before 9 o'clock. That is 8:45.

qa.q: Meena's dance class starts at 5 o'clock and lasts 15 minutes. When does it end?
qa.e: 15 minutes after 5 o'clock is quarter past 5.

qa.q: When the long hand is on 4, how many minutes past the hour is it?
qa.e: Each number is 5 minutes. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20.

qa.q: A train leaves at half past 10. Kabir reaches the station at quarter past 10. Is he early or late?
qa.e: Quarter past 10 (10:15) comes before half past 10 (10:30). He is 15 minutes early.

qa.q: Where does the long hand point at 5 o'clock?
qa.e: At o'clock times the long hand is on 12.

qa.q: At half past 7, where is the short hand?
qa.e: Half an hour after 7, the short hand has moved halfway to 8.

qa.q: At quarter past 3, where is the long hand?
qa.e: 15 minutes past means the long hand is on 3.

qa.q: Which is a sensible time to eat breakfast?
qa.e: Breakfast is in the morning.

qa.q: Which activity fits 9:00 at night?
qa.e: 9 at night is bedtime for most children.

qa.q: To show 10 o'clock, where should the short hand point?
qa.e: The short hand points to the hour.

qa.q: At half past 4, where is the long hand?
qa.e: 30 minutes past means the long hand is on 6.

qa.q: Ravi's timetable: homework at 4:00, play at 5:00. How long is homework time?
qa.e: From 4 to 5 is 1 hour.

qa.q: Which takes about 2 minutes?
qa.e: Brushing teeth takes a couple of minutes.

qa.q: Which lasts for months?
qa.e: Winter lasts a few months.

qa.q: The long hand moves from 12 to 3. How many minutes passed?
qa.e: 3 numbers × 5 minutes = 15.

qa.q: The long hand moves from 12 to 8. How many minutes passed?
What can you do in 1 minute?
qa.e: Clapping is quick. The others take much longer.

qa.q: About how long does a bath take?
qa.e: A bath usually takes some minutes.

qa.q: Reading time: 7:00 to 7:20. How many minutes?
qa.e: From 7:00 to 7:20 is 20 minutes.

qa.q: The long hand moves from 3 to 9. How many minutes passed?
qa.e: 6 numbers × 5 = 30 minutes.

qa.q: A digital clock shows 3:30. What time is it?
qa.e: 30 minutes past 3 is half past 3.

qa.q: How would a digital clock show quarter past 8?
qa.e: 15 minutes past 8 is 8:15.

qa.q: How would a digital clock show quarter to 6?
qa.e: 15 minutes before 6 is 5:45.

qa.q: Which clock uses hands?
qa.e: Analog clocks have hands.

qa.q: A sand timer runs out in 2 minutes. Raju turns it 3 times, one after another. How long in all?
qa.e: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 minutes.

qa.q: What does 12:00 on a digital clock at lunch time mean?
qa.e: 00 minutes past 12 is 12 o'clock.

qa.q: How do we check how long our homemade sand timer runs?
qa.e: A clock tells how many minutes the sand takes.

qa.q: A digital clock shows 10:05. How many minutes past 10?
qa.e: 05 means 5 minutes past.

qa.q: Which is symmetrical?
qa.e: A butterfly's wings match on both sides.

qa.q: What does symmetrical mean?
qa.a: One half matches the other half
qa.e: Both halves are the same, like mirror images.

qa.q: A bangle stall has bangles in the pattern red, gold, red, gold... What kind of pattern is it?
qa.e: Red, gold repeats again and again.

qa.q: Which is NOT symmetrical?
qa.e: G does not match if folded.

qa.q: Tiles on a fair path go: square, triangle, square, triangle. What comes next?
qa.e: The pattern repeats square, triangle.

qa.q: A symmetrical shape is folded on its line of symmetry. How many matching halves do you get?
qa.e: Two halves that match.

qa.q: Which fair item is often symmetrical?
qa.e: Masks are made with matching left and right sides.

qa.q: A carpet has the pattern ⭐🔷⭐🔷⭐🔷. How many stars are there?
qa.e: ⭐ appears 3 times.

qa.q: Which mala is symmetrical?
qa.e: R B R reads the same from both ends.

qa.q: Which mala is NOT symmetrical?
qa.e: R R B B read backwards is B B R R.

qa.q: A mala has 5 beads: R B ? B R. What colour must the middle be?
qa.e: The middle bead has no partner, so any colour keeps it symmetrical.

qa.q: With 3 red and 2 blue beads in a row, how many symmetrical malas can be made?
qa.e: R B R B R and B R R R B.

qa.q: A mala starts R B Y. To make it symmetrical with 6 beads, what are the last three?
qa.e: The second half mirrors the first: R B Y Y B R.

qa.q: How many beads are there in R B R B R?
qa.e: Count them: 5 beads.

qa.q: In the symmetrical mala B R R R B, how many red beads?
qa.e: There are 3 Rs.

qa.q: Is R R B R R symmetrical?
qa.e: Read backwards it is R R B R R.

qa.q: How can you check if a rangoli is symmetrical?
qa.a: Trace it, fold it, and see if the halves match
qa.e: Matching halves on folding show symmetry.

qa.q: What is the line that splits a design into two matching halves called?
qa.e: That fold line is the line of symmetry.

qa.q: A dot is 3 squares to the right of the fold. Where is its partner?
qa.e: Same distance on the other side.

qa.q: One half of a kolam has 6 dots. How many dots in the full symmetrical kolam (none on the fold)?
Which is a good way to draw your own symmetrical rangoli?
qa.a: Draw one half, then copy it mirrored
qa.e: Mirroring one half makes the halves match.

qa.q: Which thing around you is usually symmetrical?
qa.e: Windows usually have matching halves.

qa.q: A half-rangoli shows a petal touching the fold line. In the full design, the petal…
qa.a: Is mirrored on the other side
qa.e: Everything is mirrored across the fold.

qa.q: A rangoli has 4 lines of symmetry. Riya found 3. How many more should she look for?
You wink your right eye at a mirror. Which eye winks in the mirror image?
qa.e: A mirror swaps left and right.

qa.q: An arrow points to the right. How does it look in a mirror beside it?
qa.e: Left and right swap.

qa.q: When is a mask symmetrical?
qa.e: Matching halves make it symmetrical.

qa.q: A mask has 3 dots on its left cheek. How many on the right cheek for symmetry?
qa.e: Same as the left: 3.

qa.q: Put a mirror along the middle of half a heart. What do you see?
qa.e: The mirror shows the other half.

qa.q: Which word looks the SAME in a mirror held to the side?
qa.e: T and O are symmetrical, and TOOT reads the same backwards.

qa.q: In a mirror, does your head appear at the top or the bottom?
qa.e: A standing mirror swaps left and right, not top and bottom.

qa.q: A mask's left half has 2 horns and 1 eye. The right half has 2 horns and 2 eyes. Is it symmetrical?
qa.e: The eyes do not match.

qa.q: In a row of 6 boxes, box 2 is coloured. Which box number must be coloured to mirror it?
qa.e: Box 2 is 2nd from the left, so its partner is 2nd from the right: box 5.

qa.q: In a row of 8 boxes, box 1 is coloured. Which box number mirrors it?
qa.e: 1st from the left ↔ 1st from the right.

qa.q: Left has 6 balls, right has 2. How many should move from left to right?
qa.e: 8 in all, 4 each. Move 6 − 4 = 2.

qa.q: Odd one out: square, rectangle, circle, triangle. Which reason is right for the circle?
qa.e: The others all have corners.

qa.q: Odd one out: A, H, F, T. Which one is not symmetrical?
qa.e: A, H and T match when folded down the middle. F does not.

qa.q: A 3 by 3 grid has the middle column as the fold line. The top-left box is coloured. Which box mirrors it?
qa.e: Same row, other side of the fold.

qa.q: Left: 3 red balls, right: 3 red balls. Do the sides match?
qa.e: Both sides have the same.

qa.q: Left has 10 balls and right has 4. After moving, each side has the same. How many on each side?
Which shape leaves gaps when tiling?
qa.e: Circles cannot fit together without gaps.

qa.q: What does tiling mean?
qa.a: Covering a space with no gaps or overlaps
qa.e: Tiles fit edge to edge.

qa.q: A path goes ⬛🔺⬛🔺⬛🔺. What is the repeating unit?
qa.e: Square then triangle repeats.

qa.q: How many small square tiles cover a path 5 tiles long and 2 tiles wide?
Two equal triangles cut from a square are joined back. What tile do they make?
qa.e: The two halves rebuild the square.

qa.q: A pattern's unit is red, blue, blue. How many blues in 4 units?
qa.e: 2 blues per unit × 4 = 8.

qa.q: Which cut-out fills a square hole with no gap?
qa.a: A square of the same size
qa.e: Only a same-size square fits exactly.

qa.q: Which shape is often seen in honeycomb tiling?
qa.e: Bees make 6-sided cells that fit together.

qa.q: The giant wheel is between the food stall and the toy stall. Where is it?
qa.a: In the middle of the two
qa.e: Between means in the middle.

qa.q: Which question is a yes/no question?
qa.e: It can only be answered yes or no.

qa.q: There are 8 stalls. After the answer to 'Is it on the left half?', how many choices remain?
qa.e: Half of 8 is 4.

qa.q: Sunil's stall is opposite the ice-cream stall. What does that mean?
qa.a: It faces the ice-cream stall across the path
qa.e: Opposite means facing across.

qa.q: A clue: 'It is next to the gate and not the shoe stall.' The stalls next to the gate are shoes and bangles. Which is it?
qa.e: Next to the gate and not shoes leaves bangles.

qa.q: 16 places. Each good question halves the choices. How many questions to get to 1?
qa.e: 16 → 8 → 4 → 2 → 1: 4 questions.

qa.q: Which is the BEST first question to find a stall among 10?
qa.a: Is it on the left side of the fair?
qa.e: It rules out about half the stalls at once.

qa.q: A seat on the giant wheel is the 3rd from the top on the right side. What helps you find it?
qa.a: Counting from the top on the right side
qa.e: Follow the description exactly.

qa.q: What is a map?
qa.a: A drawing of a place seen from above
qa.e: Maps show places as seen from above.

qa.q: Which direction word tells you to change the way you are facing?
qa.e: 'Turn left' or 'turn right' changes your direction. 'Forward' keeps it the same.

qa.q: Riya walks forward, then turns left. Which hand side did she turn towards?
qa.e: Turning left means towards your left hand.

qa.q: A route: 'From the gate, go forward to the well, then turn right.' What is the landmark?
qa.e: The well is the place where you turn.

qa.q: A map shows: Gate → Kites → Food → Rides in a straight line. Walking forward from the gate, which stall comes second?
qa.e: First kites, then food.

qa.q: Which directions are better?
qa.a: Go forward to the giant wheel and turn left
qa.e: Clear directions use landmarks and turn words.

qa.q: Raju faces the gate. The food stall is on his right. He turns around. Where is the food stall now?
qa.e: Turning around swaps left and right.

qa.q: From home, Sita goes forward 3 blocks, turns right and goes 2 blocks. How many blocks did she walk?
What should you do at a dead end in a maze?
qa.a: Go back to the last turn and try another way
qa.e: Going back lets you try a new path.

qa.q: What is a landmark?
qa.a: Something easy to notice that helps you find the way
qa.e: Landmarks like a well or a big tree help describe a route.

qa.q: A maze has 4 paths from the start. 3 are dead ends. How many reach the exit?
Which is a clear route description?
qa.a: Turn right at the balloon stall, then left at the well
qa.e: It names turns and landmarks.

qa.q: Mohan passed the swings, the well and the balloon stall. How many landmarks did he pass?
qa.e: Swings, well, balloon stall: 3.

qa.q: Why can starting from the exit help?
qa.a: You can see which paths lead to it
qa.e: Tracing back shows the connected path.

qa.q: A route: right, left, left. Reena did right, left, right. How many turns did she get correct?
qa.e: First right ✔, then left ✔, then right ✘.

qa.q: To reach the exit, you need 5 turns. You have made 3. How many more?
Visitors at fair stalls: Pottery 12, Bangles 8, Food 15, Toys 10. Which stall had the most visitors?
qa.e: 15 is the biggest number in the table, so the Food stall had the most visitors.

qa.q: Stall visitors: Pottery 12, Bangles 8, Food 15, Toys 10. Which stall had the fewest visitors?
qa.e: 8 is the smallest number, so the Bangles stall had the fewest visitors.

qa.q: The Pottery stall had 12 visitors and the Toys stall had 10. How many more people visited Pottery?
qa.e: Find the difference: 12 − 10 = 2.

qa.q: Stall visitors: Pottery 12, Bangles 8, Food 15, Toys 10. How many visitors in all?
Meena kept a tally of balloons sold. It has 3 bundles of five and 2 single lines. How many balloons were sold?
qa.e: 3 bundles of five make 15. 2 more lines make 17.

qa.q: Why do we put data in a table?
qa.a: To read and compare it easily
qa.e: A table keeps the data neat, so we can quickly read it and compare.

qa.q: Favourite fair food: Chaat 9, Jalebi 7, Kulfi 9. Which sentence is true?
qa.a: Chaat and Kulfi are liked equally
qa.e: Chaat and Kulfi both got 9 votes, so they are liked equally. Jalebi got the fewest.

qa.q: Favourite rides: Giant wheel 14, Toy train 9. How many more children chose the Giant wheel?
qa.e: 14 − 9 = 5. Count on from 9: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 is 5 steps.

qa.q: Key: 🍦 = 2 ice creams. Row: 🍦🍦🍦🍦. How many ice creams?
qa.e: Each 🍦 means 2. Four pictures: 2, 4, 6, 8.

qa.q: Key: 🎈 = 5 balloons. Row: 🎈🎈🎈. How many balloons?
qa.e: Each 🎈 means 5. Three pictures: 5, 10, 15.

qa.q: What does the key in a pictograph tell us?
qa.e: The key tells how many things one picture stands for.

qa.q: Key: 🧸 = 10 toys. The toy stall's row is 🧸🧸🧸🧸. How many toys were sold?
qa.e: Each 🧸 means 10. Four pictures: 10, 20, 30, 40.

qa.q: Key: 🪁 = 2 kites. Riya sold 12 kites. How many 🪁 pictures are in her row?
qa.e: Each picture is 2 kites. Count by 2s to 12: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. That is 6 pictures.

qa.q: Key: ⭐ = 5. Kabir has ⭐⭐⭐ and Aisha has ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐. How many more does Aisha have?
qa.e: Kabir has 15 and Aisha has 25. 25 − 15 = 10. Or: 2 more stars × 5 = 10.

qa.q: Key: 🍎 = 3 apples. Row: 🍎🍎🍎🍎🍎. How many apples?
qa.e: Each 🍎 means 3. Five pictures: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15.

qa.q: Key: 🧁 = 4 cupcakes. Monday: 🧁🧁. Tuesday: 🧁🧁🧁. How many cupcakes in all?
qa.e: There are 5 pictures in all, and each is 4 cupcakes. 5 × 4 = 20.

What is 20 ÷ 4?
24 bangles are packed with 4 bangles in each box. How many boxes are needed?
qa.e: Make groups of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24. That is 6 groups. 24 ÷ 4 = 6.

qa.q: Which multiplication fact helps to find 15 ÷ 3?
qa.e: 3 × 5 = 15 tells us that 15 shared into 3 groups gives 5 each. So 15 ÷ 3 = 5.

qa.q: Kabir has 14 balloons. He ties them in bunches of 2. How many bunches does he make?
qa.e: Count by 2s to 14: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. That is 7 bunches.

qa.q: 30 people want to ride the toy train. Each coach holds 10 people. How many coaches will be filled?
qa.e: Make groups of 10: 10, 20, 30. That is 3 coaches. 30 ÷ 10 = 3.
